cards.explanation: The answer is True. The letter says, “On many past occasions and in many different ways, God spoke to our fathers through the prophets.” (Hebrews 1:1) Many times, many ways, and the prophets carried the words. That's the opening act before the big turn in the next verse.

The answer is His Son. The letter says, “But in these last days He has spoken to us by His Son…” (Hebrews 1:2) After all those prophets, God speaks by the Son Himself. I think that's the turn the whole opening hangs on.
The answer is heir. The verse says God appointed His Son “…heir of all things…” (Hebrews 1:2) All things, friends. I've got one bakery and one cookie planet, so "all things" is a little over my head.

The answer is True. The verse says God appointed Him heir, “…and through whom He made the universe.” (Hebrews 1:2) So the Son is heir of all things and the one the universe was made through. That's a long way from my little planet and my ovens.

The answer is all things. The letter says the Son is “…upholding all things by His powerful word.” (Hebrews 1:3) Not one thing, not a few, all of it. I can barely keep my own hat from sliding on a windy day.

The answer is that He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty. The verse says, “After He had provided purification for sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.” (Hebrews 1:3) The order matters, friends: purification first, then the sitting. I think that's a verse worth reading slowly.

The answer is False. The Son isn't on the angels' level. The letter says, “So He became as far superior to the angels as the name He has inherited is excellent beyond theirs.” (Hebrews 1:4) The name He inherited is more excellent than theirs. The writer goes on to back that up with what God said.

The answer is “You are My Son…” The writer asks which of the angels God ever told that line (Hebrews 1:5). It's asked as a question, and no angel is named as the one it was said to. Those words belong to the Son.
The answer is worship Him. When God brings His firstborn into the world, He says, “Let all God’s angels worship Him.” (Hebrews 1:6) ALL of them, friends. Not just a few.

The answer is servants. The verse says, “He makes His angels winds, His servants flames of fire.” (Hebrews 1:7) The writer sets that next to what God says about the Son. And at the end of the chapter he calls the angels ministering spirits sent to serve.

The answer is True. God says about the Son, “Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom.” (Hebrews 1:8) Forever and ever, friends. No end to that throne in the text.

The answer is that God anointed Him with the oil of joy. The verse says, “therefore God, Your God, has anointed You above Your companions with the oil of joy.” (Hebrews 1:9) The word “therefore” ties it to the Son loving righteousness and hating wickedness. Above His companions, too.
The answer is False. The line says, “…the heavens are the work of Your hands.” (Hebrews 1:10) That's the Lord's hands, not the angels'. The same line has Him laying the foundations of the earth.

The answer is that He remains the same. The line says, “They will perish, but You remain…” (Hebrews 1:11) and then, “but You remain the same, and Your years will never end.” (Hebrews 1:12) The heavens change like a garment, and He doesn't.

The answer is enemies. God says, “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet…” (Hebrews 1:13) The writer asks which of the angels was ever told that. Sit at My right hand is not an angel's line in this passage.

The answer is those who will inherit salvation. The writer asks, “Are not the angels ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation?” (Hebrews 1:14) So the angels are sent to serve them. That's the angels' job description in this verse.

The answer is True. The verse says, “We must pay closer attention, therefore, to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away.” (Hebrews 2:1) Closer attention, so we do not drift away. That “so that” tells us why the attention matters.

The answer is binding. The verse says, “For if the message spoken by angels was binding, and every transgression and disobedience received its just punishment…” (Hebrews 2:2) The “if” sets up the big question in the next verse. A binding message is one that holds.

The answer is False. The writer asks, “…how shall we escape if we neglect such a great salvation?” (Hebrews 2:3) He doesn't offer any way out for neglect. That's why he said earlier to pay closer attention.

The answer is those who heard Him. The verse says this salvation “…was first announced by the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard Him…” (Hebrews 2:3) So the Lord announced it first, and those who heard Him confirmed it to us. The writer includes himself in that “us.”

The answer is through signs and wonders and miracles. The verse says it was “…affirmed by God through signs, wonders, various miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit…” (Hebrews 2:4) That's God's own affirming. The gifts of the Holy Spirit are named right alongside the signs.

The answer is True. The verse says God affirmed it with “…gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to His will.” (Hebrews 2:4) According to His will, friends. The gifts are handed out the way He chooses.
